answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every new participant to anchor a time-locked collateral deposit before routing transactions through its node. The network topology maps each agent as a vertex in a bounded credit graph, where transaction throughput is constrained by historical peer endorsements rather than raw address creation. In this structure, deploying a farm of fake identities creates a sable cloud of unverified accounts that cannot route volume without locking substantial capital at each point, making mass identity replication financially unprofitable.
